examples.text: an onshore breeze

examples.text: Princeton University's Center for Environmental Studies recommended today that New Jersey minimize adverse impacts of offshore drilling by limiting to the Atlantic City area any onshore bases built to support and supply oil rigs in the ocean.

glosses: Within the country; not overseas.

examples.text: By this measure, it was only the second largest onshore leak in the US last year, surpassed by one near San Antonio, Texas in March which discharged 147 tonnes of methane an hour.

glosses: From the sea towards the land.

examples.text: Like most storms, Hurricane Katrina weakened as it came onshore, and by Monday evening the National Hurricane Center had downgraded it to a tropical storm.

glosses: To relocate production, services or jobs to lower-cost locations in the same country.

examples.text: I don’t want to suggest that any attempt to onshore production will doom America to runaway costs, supply-chain catastrophes, and frayed global alliances. glosses: Changer la localisation de quelque chose.

examples.text: Le centre a organisé trois mini camps de 14 enfants, un dans le jardin de Ker Avel, un autre relocalisé à Saint-Jean-du-Doigt à cause des incendies, et un dernier qui a pu finalement se passer à Sizun.

glosses: Rapatrier une production industrielle qui avait été délocalisée.

examples.text: Le fabricant de ski Rossignol a annoncé qu’il allait « relocaliser » des emplois en France. […] Rossignol va rapatrier d’ici janvier la production de 60000 paires de ski de Taïwan à Sallanches en Haute-Savoie.
